transcript: I attended the second preview of a brand new musical called Saturday Church at New York Theatre Workshop, and it's certainly a work in progress. This show is getting a lot of buzz, rightfully so when you have creators like James Ijames, Whitney White, and Sia attached to it. It's more or less about a Black, queer teenager named Ulysses living in New York and straddling two different worlds and sets of expectations placed on him by his family and his newfound community. Overall, I thought it was a lot of fun and the talent in this cast is just undeniable. With folks like J. Harrison Ghee and Joaquina Kaluganko, you know before it even starts that you're in for a vocal feast. And the music was definitely the highlight for me, with a great sound design to support it. Everything was sonically crisp, and all the genres blended throughout this piece worked quite well for this space and these performers. I also loved the design elements like the lighting, sets and costumes which were detailed and very aesthetically pleasing. The actual storytelling was uneven for me, especially in Act 2 where I felt it wasn't focused enough. I think numerous characters don't have the ability to fully develop, so I'm wondering if maybe there are too many of them. Like I said, it's still a work in progress, but I really think they have something here. It's a good concept and they have the right people working on it, so I am excited for this to cook a little more. With that, another program for my collection.
